clue.text: Dress to kill, securing male's love

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly inside, so the killing phrase wraps round the male letter

parts.note: to do in is slang for to kill
M is the standard abbreviation for male
love is nil in tennis, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A femme fatale's outfit chosen to ensnare a man's affections.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a loose hooded cloak worn with a mask at a masquerade, so a kind of costume.

clue.text: Source of nightmares has fellow clutching top of leg in terror

indicators.note: in means the fellow with his catch goes inside the word for terror

parts.note: dread is terror

indicators.note: clutching means holding on to, so the fellow grips the next letter within

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A frightening scene in which a man grabs someone's leg in terror.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'clutching' sets the leg's first letter inside the fellow, and 'in' sets that pair inside the word for terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamland is the world of sleep and dreams, where bad dreams come from.

clue.text: Measures? The writer misleads, excluding kilo

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter as me

indicators.note: excluding means leaving out the kilo letter

parts.note: tricks means misleads

explanation.surface: A writer's deceptive measurements quietly leave out the kilos.
explanation.definitionFit: Metrics are standards of measurement or quantified indicators; the question mark marks a plural noun read from a verb-like word.

clue.text: What could be uneasier than a nervous condition?

indicators.note: could be says these letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks what is worse than a nervous condition, a sly nod to feeling uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurasthenia is an old diagnosis for nervous exhaustion with fatigue and anxiety.

clue.text: Historic military forces chaplain

parts.note: historic things belong to the past
OR stands for Other Ranks, the enlisted soldiers of the British army

explanation.surface: A clergyman who served with the armed forces in times gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are Christian ministers who look after a flock; a chaplain serves an institution, a pastor a congregation.

clue.text: Former student, advanced student, group of students? Expression of doubt creeps in

indicators.note: creeps in means slipping quietly into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: L, a learner, is the student driver's plate letter
NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK students' body
um is a hesitant noise of doubt

explanation.surface: A list of students past and present, with a hesitant pause slipping in.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a graduate or former pupil of a school or university.

clue.text: Satisfactory year in middle of pastoral capital city

indicators.note: in means the satisfactory year goes inside the central pair
the middle of an eight-letter word is its central pair of letters

parts.note: OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: A decent year spent in the heart of the countryside, then the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital of Japan, a capital city.

clue.text: Back under control, less disorderly after uprising, with King installed

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
after uprising means the word goes up the down light, read in reverse

parts.note: neater means tidier, less disorderly
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: After a rebellion, a king put back on the throne restores order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after uprising' turns NEATER into RETAEN, and 'installed' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something retaken has been captured again, so brought back under control.

clue.text: Centre of spreading illness cleared? Awesome

indicators.note: centre of points to the middle four letters of the word for the outbreak
cleared means those middle letters are emptied out

parts.note: an epidemic is a disease spreading widely

explanation.surface: The heart of a spreading disease is eliminated, which is awesome news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of' and 'cleared' together take DEMI out of EPIDEMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic is slang for impressive or tremendous, a casual synonym of awesome.

clue.text: Range not initially including source of legendary guitar accessory

indicators.note: including means the shortened range takes another letter inside it
not initially means the word for range loses its opening letter

parts.note: a spectrum is a full range of something

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A legendary guitarist's pick, part of a whole range of gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' trims SPECTRUM to PECTRUM; 'including' puts the L from 'legendary' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plectrum is the small flat pick used to pluck guitar strings, a standard accessory for players.

clue.text: Shakespearean flourish? Reduced returns — dark theatre tonight, ultimately

indicators.note: returns means the word for reduced comes back, read right to left

parts.note: something reduced has been cut

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A theatre is dark tonight, with takings cut, so no flourish at curtain-up.
explanation.walkthrough: A dark theatre is one with no show on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucket is an old word for a trumpet fanfare, found in Shakespeare's stage directions; the question mark flags the archaic term.

clue.text: It's enormous, horrific, origin of someone's lack of bravery

indicators.note: horrific suggests something mangled into a frightful new shape
the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A timid person faced with something huge and horrific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrific' rearranges ITSENORMOUS into TIMOROUSNES; the S from 'someone's' finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Timorousness means nervousness and fearfulness, so a want of courage.

clue.text: Cracking material with a sequence of opening numbers

definitions.text: Cracking material with a sequence of opening numbers

parts.words: Cracking material with a sequence of opening numbers
parts.note: a safecracker's target is a fastening opened by dialling the right series of digits

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking material' suggests excellent cloth, but it means something a burglar tries to crack, and the 'opening numbers' are the digits that open it.
explanation.definitionFit: A padlock or safe dial secured by a code of numbers entered in the right order.

clue.text: Voice, strained, to falter, though one escapes fight

indicators.note: escapes means the letter for one gets out of the verb for faltering

parts.note: to fail is to falter or weaken
I is the Roman numeral for one
a set-to is a brief fight or scrap

explanation.surface: A singer's voice, under strain, starts to falter as a quarrel breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strained' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition. FAIL loses its I to give FAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the high, forced head voice above a man's normal range, which sounds strained.

clue.text: Earlier time for holy man's character flaw

indicators.note: earlier means the letter for time moves further forward in the word

parts.note: a saint is a holy man

explanation.surface: Even a holy man, earlier in his life, might have had a flaw in his character.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a blemish on someone's reputation or moral record, so a flaw of character.

clue.text: A railway brings in one cultivating the big guns?

indicators.note: brings in means the railway pieces take the next piece inside

parts.note: a tiller is someone who tills, cultivating the soil

explanation.surface: A railway carries in a farmer, who is perhaps a big player.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is heavy guns collectively; the question mark flags the idiom read literally.

clue.text: Cool guy is accommodating of French trainee

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the cool guy holds the French word inside

parts.note: a cat is jazz slang for a cool man
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A laid-back man is putting up a French apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training for the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Wreath in Alpine house including primrose at the front

indicators.note: including means the house takes in another letter

parts.note: a chalet is a wooden house in the Alps

indicators.note: at the front means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A floral wreath hangs in a mountain chalet, with primrose leading the display.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a garland or wreath worn on the head.

clue.text: Colourful spot set up to house large and small child

indicators.note: to house means to hold inside
set up means raised, so in a down light the word reads upwards

parts.note: a red dot is a coloured spot

explanation.surface: A spotty rash on a toddler, setting a parent's mind racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns REDDOT into TODDER; 'to house' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler is a young child just learning to walk.

clue.text: Look at cut involving standard computer material — it's outrageous

indicators.note: involving means the shortened word wraps round the next pieces
cut means the word for look at loses its final letter

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
a norm is a standard
IT, information technology, is the stuff of computing

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing a pay cut that hits standard computer kit finds it outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the last letter of the looking word, leaving EY, which 'involving' wraps round the other two pieces. The definition reads as a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity is a monstrous wrong, so the thing that is outrageous; the definition reads as a noun phrase.

clue.text: Go around, taking article into repairman

indicators.note: into means the article is placed inside the repairman's word

parts.note: a mender is someone who repairs
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A repairman wanders around, carrying a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander on a winding course, roaming around.

clue.text: Top-grade education curtailed and mark granted? That's novel

parts.note: A is the top grade in exams

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, losing the last letter

parts.note: studying is a form of education
a scar is a mark left on the skin
to let is to allow or grant

explanation.surface: A top-grade schooling cut short and a mark awarded: a story in itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Conan Doyle's first Sherlock Holmes story is a novel, here pointed at by the phrase.

clue.text: A shade quiet in Germany? Just a bit

indicators.note: Just a bit says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question whether a calm Germany might be just a touch of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour, a faint shade.

clue.text: Hard drinker served up moonshine

indicators.note: served up means delivered upwards, reading the pieces in reverse in a down light

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a sot is a habitual drinker

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker is handed home-brewed spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moonshine' suggests bootleg liquor, but here it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine also means foolish talk, and tosh is British slang for nonsense.

clue.text: Individual restricted by friend heading off could become this

definitions.text: Individual restricted by friend heading off could become this

indicators.note: restricted by means the individual is hemmed in by the shortened friend
heading off means the word for friend loses its first letter

parts.note: an ally is a friend
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A person cut off as a friend departs may well end up isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: ALLY 'heading off' gives LLY, which surrounds ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose friend leaves is likely to feel solitary and without company.

clue.text: Female scoundrel, say, embracing Duke without much thought

indicators.note: embracing means holding the next letter within

parts.note: a heel is a scoundrel; adding the feminine ending gives a playful word for a woman cad, flagged as made up by say

explanation.surface: A villainous woman has a duke in her arms, acting without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means careless or reckless, acting with no regard or attention.

clue.text: That man is enthralled by right-wing notion

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive within, so the man sits inside the right-winger

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, a right-winger
he is that man

explanation.surface: A man captivated by a conservative idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an idea or proposed explanation, so a notion.

clue.text: A second attempt to bring in one off-course

indicators.note: to bring in means the attempt takes the next letter inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A second try is made to rescue someone who has wandered off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means away from the proper path, so wandering off-course.
